waypoints.name: Oberjoch
waypoints.advice: 113 km in you reach Oberjoch. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Garmisch Partenkirchen, mostly downhill.

waypoints.advice: Garmisch Partenkirchen closes the day.

sections.advice: Lindau → Oberstaufen is 32 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Oberstaufen → Oberjoch climbs about 1178 m in 39 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Oberjoch → Garmisch Partenkirchen drops about 1178 m over 62 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: German Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: For 41 km this is German Alpine Road, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Oberstaufen → Oberjoch
scenicChapters.narrative: A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not. The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 50 km. 1178 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall.

scenicChapters.title: Romantische Strasse
scenicChapters.narrative: 79 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

german-alpine-road-lindau-garmisch-parte.story: A 170 km one-way ride from near Lindau, about 2 h 47 of riding. The stops in between: Oberstaufen and Oberjoch. The highest point is about 1,550 m. Oberjoch is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Germany into Austria - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
